Describe the concept of division of labour among the different types of cells in human trachea in any TWO points.

Division of labour means that specialised cells cooperate by performing different functions. Goblet cells secrete mucus that traps particles and microbes. Ciliated epithelial cells sweep the mucus towards the throat.
Award credit for the concept and relevant examples that link a tracheal cell type to its function. Naming a cell without its role is incomplete.

Shoaib conducted an experiment to determine the effect of a fertiliser on the growth of plants. He used four pots with different species of plants and varying amounts of soil and fertiliser for his experiment. However, he could not obtain the required result. Identify any THREE errors in his experimental set-up.

The pots contained different plant species, and the amount of soil differed. The design did not identify a no-fertiliser control. If the experiment is testing the presence of fertiliser, apply the same measured dose to each treatment pot. If testing different doses, dose can vary deliberately while the other conditions stay constant.
One mark per valid design error, up to three. The notes discuss unequal amounts of fertiliser. A planned dose series is valid if other variables are controlled and a zero-dose group is included.

Complete the given table by mentioning the demerits of kingdom classification systems.

| Classification System | Demerit |
| --- | --- |
| Two-kingdom classification system | 1. …  2. … |
| Five-kingdom classification system | 1. … |

Two-kingdom system: it does not separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes, and it groups fungi with plants despite their different nutrition. Five-kingdom system: it does not place acellular viruses in a kingdom.
One mark for each of two distinct limitations of the two-kingdom system, and one mark for a limitation of the five-kingdom system.

The given diagram represents an alveolus and blood capillary. X represents a gas molecule.

i. Identify molecule X. (1 mark)
ii. What would be the effect of rigorous exercise on the concentration of molecule X in the human body? (1 mark)
iii. Why is the percentage composition of molecule X in alveolar air different from the atmospheric air? (1 mark)

i. Carbon dioxide (CO₂).
ii. Working muscles produce more CO₂ as their rate of respiration increases. In healthy people ventilation also rises, so arterial CO₂ need not stay elevated.
iii. CO₂ diffuses from the blood into alveolar air, increasing its proportion relative to atmospheric air.
One mark each for identifying carbon dioxide, explaining increased CO₂ production during vigorous exercise, and explaining why alveolar air contains more CO₂ than atmospheric air.
How can change in the pH beyond the optimum level affect the structure of enzyme? Describe in TWO points.

A pH change alters the charges on amino-acid side chains and can disrupt interactions such as ionic bonds and hydrogen bonds. A large change can distort the enzyme’s three-dimensional structure and active site, reducing substrate binding and activity.
One mark for each of two valid points. Link the pH change to the structural change and its effect on the active site.

Describe structural adaptations in any THREE of the permanent tissues in plants that help to perform their function efficiently.

Epidermis: closely packed cells form a protective layer. Collenchyma: unevenly thickened primary cell walls support growing parts while allowing them to bend. Sclerenchyma: thick, lignified secondary walls provide rigid support.
For each of three tissues, award one mark for an adaptation and one for its corresponding function.
6b
The given diagram shows the cross-section of a leaf. Describe the structural adaptation and advantages of any THREE features present in the cross-section of the leaf shown in the given diagram.

Palisade mesophyll contains many chloroplasts near the upper surface, helping absorb light. Spongy mesophyll has intercellular air spaces that allow gases to diffuse through the leaf. The upper epidermis is transparent, letting light reach the photosynthetic cells beneath.
For each of three visible features, award one mark for the structural adaptation and one for its advantage.

Sara is 25 years old and spends most of her time studying in a library. Her brother Zia is 15 years old and spends most of his time playing with friends. They consume same quality and quantity of food. Zia is lean and Sara is overweight. With reference to the energy requirement and consumption of both Sara and Zia,

i. identify THREE factors that cause the difference in their weight. (3 marks)
ii. describe each of the factor identified in part i. (3 marks)

Physical activity: Zia’s playing can use more energy than sedentary study. Age and growth: a growing teenager may need more energy to support new tissues. Sex and body composition: average lean mass and energy needs can differ, although the needs of these two individuals cannot be inferred precisely. Eating the same amount can result in different energy balances.
One mark each for identifying age, activity and sex or gender in the context of the question, and one each for linking the factor to energy needs.
7b

The given schematic diagram represents one of the processes in plants.

i. Identify the mechanism that is depicted in the given diagram. (1 mark)
ii. Describe the identified mechanism in FIVE points. (5 marks)

i. The pressure-flow mechanism of phloem translocation.
ii. (1) Sucrose is loaded into phloem at the source. (2) The solute lowers the water potential, drawing water in from xylem by osmosis. (3) This raises hydrostatic pressure at the source. (4) The pressure difference drives sap towards the sink. (5) Sucrose is unloaded at the sink, allowing water to return to xylem.
One mark for identifying pressure flow, then one mark per valid stage, up to five.
